title: Compatible strict residue extensions and descent of weak solutions
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings (DVRs) [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension] and residue fields $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Local means pulling back the target maximal ideal to the source maximal ideal. For an injective local map $U\to V$ of DVRs with fraction fields $F\subseteq G$, a finite extension $H/F$ is a weak solution if the following holds. Let $R$ be the integral closure of $U$ in $H$ and $C$ the integral closure of $V$ in $(G\otimes_FH)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every maximal ideal $q$ of $C$, $n=q\cap R$ is maximal, $R_n,C_q$ are DVRs, and $nC_q=qC_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here $\mathrm{red}$ means quotient by all nilpotents and finite means finite-dimensional over the base field. There exists a commutative square of injective local maps $A\to A_s$, $B\to B_s$, $A_s\to B_s$ of DVRs. The fraction field extensions $\operatorname{Frac}(A_s)/K$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(B_s)/L$ are separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. The induced residue extensions $k_s/k$ and $l_s/l$ are separable closures [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\mathfrak m_AA_s=\mathfrak m_{A_s}$, so the image of every uniformizer of $A$ is a uniformizer of $A_s$. If, in addition, $k$ is perfect (every algebraic extension is separable; equivalently, in positive characteristic $p$, Frobenius $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective) and there exists a finite weak solution for $A_s\to B_s$, there exists a finite weak solution for $A\to B$. The square itself requires no perfectness assumption. Neither completeness, perfectness of $l$, nor any hypothesis on perfect cores is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09ET, lemma-solution-after-strict-henselization, statement (1)-(3), restricted to weak solutions, and its first proof paragraph: A_s is a filtered colimit of finite etale A-algebras with the prescribed residue closure, as in algebra.tex Tag 09E0 (lemma-colimit-finite-etale-given-residue-field); the maximal ideal is generated by the image of the original uniformizer.

proof.text: Apply the residue-closure clauses (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ at a geometric closed point. They give compatible separable closures $k_s\subseteq l_s$ extending $k\subseteq l$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] to $(B,\mathfrak m_B,l_s)$ and call its local colimit $B_s$. It is strictly henselian, its residue field is $l_s$, and $B\to B_s$ is local and ind-etale. Hence [lem-sfb-local-ind-etale-dvr] makes it an injective map of DVRs with separable algebraic fraction-field extension. No completion is taken.

Apply [lem-sfb-local-separable-residue-ind-finite-etale] to $R=A$, $E=k_s$, and the local target $S=B_s$ with its specified residue embedding $k_s\hookrightarrow l_s$. Write $A_s=\varinjlim_i A_i$ for its local colimit. The compatible local maps $A_i\to B_s$ give a local map $A_s\to B_s$, so the square commutes. By [lem-sfb-local-ind-etale-dvr], $A_s$ is a DVR, $K_s=\operatorname{Frac}(A_s)$ is separable algebraic over $K$, and $\mathfrak m_{A_s}=\pi A_s$ for any uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. The map $A_s\to B_s$ is injective: its kernel is a prime of the DVR $A_s$; the only possible nonzero prime is $(\pi)$, but $\pi$ has nonzero image since $A\to B\to B_s$ is injective. This proves all assertions about the square.

source.place: Tag 09ET first and second paragraphs, using algebra.tex Tags 09E0 and 04GT.

proof.text: For the descent clause, assume $k$ is perfect and let $H/K_s$ be a finite weak solution. The finite etale local stages $A_i$ are DVRs by [lem-sfb-local-ind-etale-dvr]; put $F_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A_i)$. Since the maps are injective and the system is directed, every ratio of elements of $A_s$ belongs to some $F_i$, so $K_s=\bigcup_iF_i$. Choose a $K_s$-basis $h_1=1,h_2,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$, and choose $i$ containing all the finitely many structure constants in $h_ah_b=\sum_c c_{abc}h_c$. The $F_i$-span $N$ of this basis in $H$ is a finite-dimensional unital subalgebra and a domain, hence a field: multiplication by any nonzero element is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional vector space and is therefore surjective. Its basis remains independent over $K_s$, so multiplication induces $K_s\otimes_{F_i}N\cong H$. Fix this $i$, and write $D=A_i$, $F=F_i$.

source.place: Tag 09ET third paragraph, finite-field descent made explicit by structure constants.

proof.text: Let $R$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $N$ and $R_s$ the integral closure of $A_s$ in $H$. The tail of the system in Step 2 presents $A_s$ as ind-etale over $D$. Therefore [lem-sfb-integral-closure-ind-etale-base-change] and Step 3 identify $R_s=A_s\otimes_D R$. Tensor associativity identifies $L_s\otimes_F N$ with $L_s\otimes_{K_s}H$; taking quotients by nilpotents respects this identification. Let $C$ be the integral closure of $B_s$ in this reduced algebra. For a maximal $q$ of $C$, put $n_s=q\cap R_s$ and $n=q\cap R$. The finite-case statements of [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], for $A_s\to B_s,H/K_s$ and $D\to B_s,N/F$, make these contractions maximal and $R_n,(R_s)_{n_s},C_q$ DVRs. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-local-ind-etale-dvr], with $U=D,T=A_s$ and coefficient algebra $R$, gives $n(R_s)_{n_s}=n_s(R_s)_{n_s}$. Since $H$ is weak, $n_sC_q=qC_q$, whence $nC_q=qC_q$. This holds for every $q$, so $N/F$ is a weak solution for $D\to B_s$.

source.place: Tag 09ET third paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 0CBF; normalization comparison replaces an implicit passage to the finite stage.

proof.text: The ring $D=A_i$ is finite etale local over $A$, and $D\to B_s$ is an injective local map to a strictly henselian DVR. The lower residue field of $A$ is perfect by the descent hypothesis retained in Step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-weak-solution-transfer] to $A\to D\to B_s$ and the weak solution $N/F$ from Step 4. Its corrected perfect-lower-residue hypothesis is thus satisfied. It gives a finite field extension $N_0/K$ weakly solving $A\to B_s$. It asserts existence of a possibly larger field $N_0$, not that the particular $N/K$ works.

source.place: Tag 09ET, final finite-etale step, with the perfect-lower-residue correction; Tag 0GLR (lemma-solution-goes-up) supplies permanence for solutions, not arbitrary weak solutions, in the supporting lemma.

proof.text: It remains to descend from $B_s$ to $B$. Put $E=(L\otimes_KN_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$, let $R_0$ normalize $A$ in $N_0$, and let $C_0$ normalize $B$ in $E$. By [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], $E$ is a nonempty finite product of finite extensions $E_j/L$, and every maximal $q$ of $C_0$ has maximal contraction $n$ in $R_0$, with $(R_0)_n,(C_0)_q$ DVRs. Apply that same node to $B\to B_s$ and each finite $E_j/L$: every such $q$ lifts to a maximal $r$ in the corresponding normalization $T_j$ of $B_s$ in $(L_s\otimes_LE_j)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The product $T=\prod_jT_j$ is the normalization of $B_s$ in $(L_s\otimes_KN_0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Indeed tensor associativity identifies the algebras after reduction: maps to any reduced algebra kill precisely the nilpotents at either intermediate reduction; and integrality in a finite product is componentwise, using the product of the finitely many monic equations. Thus $r$ is an upper normalized branch of the weak solution $N_0$ for $A\to B_s$. The inclusions induce local maps $(R_0)_n\to(C_0)_q\to T_r$.

Choose uniformizers $a,b,c$ in $(R_0)_n,(C_0)_q,T_r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], applied first in $(C_0)_q$ and then in $T_r$, write $a=ub^e$ and $b=vc^f$ with $u,v$ units and $e,f\geq1$; positivity follows because both maps are local. Units remain units under these maps. Since $N_0/K$ weakly solves $A\to B_s$, $aT_r=\mathfrak m_{T_r}=cT_r$. The displayed equations give $a=u v^e c^{ef}$, so $ef=1$: in a DVR $(c^d)=(c)$ with $d\geq1$ forces $d=1$, by cancellation and the fact that $c$ is not a unit. Thus $e=1$ and $n(C_0)_q=q(C_0)_q$. Step 6 supplied a lift for every $q$, so every normalized branch has index one. Consequently $N_0/K$ is a finite weak solution for $A\to B$, as required.

source.place: Tag 09ES proof (1), uniformizer calculation spelling out weakly-unramified descent.
